why: The record schemas for ticfac's four-operation executor protocol (SPEC §4.3), the
role-result envelope every LLM job returns (§4.4), and the evidence record a gate
persists (§10.1). Phase 0 step 3 freezes them BEFORE code moves, so the reconciler
and every executor — local subprocess, Herdr, Cloudflare Sandbox, Cloudflare
Computer — are written against one surface instead of four that happen to agree.
WHAT DRIFT THIS CATCHES. The protocol's whole value is that the reconciler does not
know which executor it is talking to. That property has no compiler behind it: an
executor is free to return a JobStatus with a field the reconciler never reads, or
to omit one it does. The failure is silent and it is a LIVENESS bug — a status
whose `terminal` flag disagrees with its `state` makes a controller either wait
forever or dispose a running workspace. So the schemas live here, with a reader on
each side, and the golden and negative documents below are the part that proves the
reader is a reader rather than a decoration.
WHY THE NEGATIVE EXAMPLES MATTER MORE THAN THE GOLDEN ONES. A schema nothing has
ever been refused by is not known to refuse anything. Every negative document below
names the refusal it expects, in the exact words both validators produce, so a
keyword quietly dropped from a schema fails a build instead of widening the
contract.
READERS (both must stay in this list):
- internal/factory/jobprotocol/contract_test.go
- cloud/factory/test/job-protocol.test.ts

versioning.rule: Every record carries schema_version and a schema_id ending in .v<n>. The reconciler validates against the schema_id a record declares, never against 'the current one'.
versioning.adding_a_field: Records are closed (additionalProperties: false), so adding a field is a new schema_id and a new schema_version — not a compatible extension. That is the opposite of the tk --json manifest's rule, and deliberately: tk publishes ONE surface many consumers read, while an executor record is exchanged between two components that ship together, where a field one side invents and the other ignores is the bug.
versioning.records_are_closed: additionalProperties: false on every record, and on every nested object except JobHandle.handle, which is executor-private by design.
versioning.schema_subset: These schemas use only the JSON Schema keywords both readers enforce: $ref (local #/$defs/<name> only), type, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, enum, anyOf, description, $comment. A keyword outside that set makes the contract fail to PARSE on both sides rather than being silently ignored.

operations.rule: Persist the JobSpec before addressing the executor, then record the returned handle. A handle that was never persisted is a job nobody can find after a restart.
Re-address by stable identity and resume from the cursor. inspect distinguishes a live worker from a missing one; it never dispatches.
Revoke credentials, THEN request a stop. A cancelled handle can never obtain a fresh credential; the refusal is durable and is checked before every boot, so a restart cannot undo it.
Read terminal facts from durable source refs and the worker's report. Terminal output is diagnostic material and never the completion contract.

credentials.$comment: Credentials are part of the protocol, not an adapter detail (SPEC §4.3). The host issues EVERY credential a job holds — model access, and source access at a declared grade — and records the grant in the attempt record. The ownership, key names and file format live in credential-ownership.json; what lives here is the shape the grant takes ON A JobSpec, and the semantics cancel must honour. The two files are cross-checked by both readers, because two spellings of one rule is exactly the drift contracts/ exists to catch.

revocation.on_cancel: revoke credentials before requesting a stop
revocation.rule: A stop is a durable refusal to issue credentials, not a revocation a restart can undo.

cost.rule: Cost is a property of the CREDENTIAL, not of the job. A metered credential carries a cost budget enforced from gateway telemetry. A flat-rate credential — a subscription seat behind a broker — has no per-request cost to bound and SAYS SO: its budget_field is required and null, so 'no budget' is a stated fact rather than a missing key. Wall-clock and cancellation still apply to it, and quota exhaustion is reported as its own failure class, never as a broken route.

completion_contract.why: SPEC §10.1. Terminal output is useful diagnostic material, but it is not a completion contract. This preserves the rule cloud/factory/src/worker-collect.ts already enforces, and it is why JobResult.source and JobResult.role_result are required while evidence output may be a bounded artifact URI.

allowed_only_after: the required source or evidence has been persisted
or an explicit recovery/escalation outcome has been recorded
disposal.why: SPEC §10.3. extensions/ticks-runner/merge.ts already refuses cleanup until tracker durability and integration ancestry are known; a remote executor and a restarted controller do not weaken the invariant.

job_spec.description: What to run: the role, the source revision, the requested capabilities, the inputs, the output contract, the artifact destination, the credential grant, and the limits. Substrate-neutral on purpose — concrete backend names never appear.

job_handle.description: A stable, opaque, re-addressable identity for a started job. Opaque to the reconciler and interpreted only by the executor that issued it; re-addressable means a controller that restarted with nothing but this record can inspect, cancel and collect.

job_status.description: Lifecycle observations and a cursor. Reports what the executor can see, not what the reconciler concludes.

cancel_ack.description: The acknowledgement cancel returns. It states that credentials were revoked, in what order relative to the stop request, and that reissue is refused — the three facts a caller cannot verify for itself.

job_result.description: Terminal facts: outcome and failure class, the source refs the job actually produced, the structured role output, and references to artifacts and evidence.

role_result.description: The fixed envelope around every role job's structured output. `result` is the role-specific contract named by schema_id, which is what JobSpec.output_schema requested; the envelope around it never varies by role.

evidence.description: A bounded, reproducible record that a configured command or review check ran against a named source ref and produced a result (SPEC §10.1). THE ONLY definition of the record in the bundle: contracts/ticfac-run-state.json places the file and pins how it is written, and references this schema_id rather than restating the shape. Its provenance fields are the shared $defs.provenance object every committed .ticfac/ record carries (SPEC §10.4). Every field is REQUIRED, nullable where it can be genuinely absent: a record that omits integration_ref and one that states it as null are different claims, and only the second is evidence.

job_id.description: run/tick/attempt identity, e.g. run-42/tick-abc/attempt-1. Opaque to the executor; the reconciler owns its shape.

role.description: SPEC §4.4. There is no universal Decision Agent: every LLM call is a bounded job with a role-specific contract, so the role is a closed vocabulary rather than free text.

executor.$comment: SPEC §4.3 initial executors. An executor NAME crosses this seam; a concrete backend name does not — that is the difference between `cloudflare-computer` here and `container-shell` in an evidence record, which explains a run after the fact.

write_ref.description: The ref the job may write. Naming it in the spec is what lets a read-only source grade be enforced by the issuer rather than trusted from the runner.

capabilities.$comment: A REQUEST, not a backend selection. The Cloudflare executor translates these to Computer Workspace and backend choices; a local executor translates the same request to a worktree and a subprocess.

max_cost_usd.description: The budget a METERED model credential is enforced against, from gateway telemetry. A flat-rate seat has nothing to enforce it against and declares budget_field: null instead — wall_seconds still binds it.

issuer.$comment: The host issues every credential a job holds. A job never presents one it brought itself, which is why this is a one-value enum rather than a free string.

issued_by_host.description: The shorthand the SPEC §4.3 illustration prints: model access is issued by the host and nothing further is pinned. Use the object form to declare cost class.

metered_cost.$comment: budget_field names the JobSpec.limits key the budget is read from, spelled exactly as credential-ownership.json spells it.

budget_field.description: REQUIRED and null. A subscription seat behind a broker has no per-request cost to bound, and the contract makes it say so rather than leaving the key out, where 'no budget' and 'budget forgotten' look identical.

source_grade.description: The grade at which the host issues source access. A closed vocabulary because the grade is the security boundary: read-only means git write is refused by the issuer, not by the runner's good manners.

write_ref_prefix.description: The only ref namespace a write grade may advance. Absent on a read-only grade.

credentials.$comment: Both halves are REQUIRED. A JobSpec that names no source grade is not 'unrestricted', it is unreviewable — nobody reading the attempt record afterwards can say what the job was allowed to touch.

output_schema.description: The role-specific contract the job's role_result.result must satisfy, e.g. ticfac.job-result.implement-tick.v1. Named in the spec so the reconciler validates against what it ASKED for, not against what came back.

handle_payload.description: Executor-private addressing. The ONE open object in this contract: a Cloudflare Computer workspace id and a local pid have nothing in common, and forcing them into a shared shape would put backend names back on the seam. Opaque to the reconciler, which stores and returns it verbatim.

state.$comment: `lost` is deliberately NOT terminal. The executor can no longer address the handle, which is a statement about the observer, not about the job: recovery may re-adopt it. Collapsing lost into failed is how a running workspace gets disposed.

terminal.description: Whether `state` can still change. Redundant with state ON PURPOSE and cross-checked by the anyOf below: a controller branches on one flag, and a disagreement between the two is a bug worth failing on rather than a field worth trusting.

cursor.description: Opaque resumption point for the observation stream. Hand it back to the next inspect to avoid re-reading; null when the executor has no more to say.

credentials_revoked.description: One permitted value. An acknowledgement that admits it did not revoke is not an acknowledgement — the caller has no other way to learn that the job still holds a live credential.

order.description: The ordering the SPEC makes a MUST. Encoded as a value rather than as two timestamps because a validator can refuse a wrong value and cannot refuse a wrong clock.

reissue.description: Durable. A kill switch is a refusal to ISSUE, checked before every boot — not a revocation a restart can undo.

salvage_deadline.description: How long bounded salvage may still run before dispose. Null when none was granted.

failure_class.$comment: quota_exhausted has its own slot because a flat-rate seat running out of quota is NOT a broken route (SPEC §4.3); reporting it as infrastructure_error sends the next repair at the wrong problem.

head_sha.description: Null when the job produced no commit — collect-vocabulary.json's `no-commits` verdict, stated as a fact rather than inferred from a missing key.

evidence_ref.$comment: How a JobResult and a RoleResult cite evidence: by the `key` of a ticfac.evidence.v1 record, which is also its filename under .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/evidence/. One identifier, so a citation can be resolved to the record it names instead of being trusted.

key.description: The `key` of the evidence record (ticfac.evidence.v1) this reference resolves to.

failure_class.description: A success cannot carry a failure class. Typed null rather than merely omitted, so a result that sets one is refused instead of ignored.

outcome_failed.$comment: A failure without a class is the record that produces 'the run broke' incident reports. Requiring it here is what makes quota_exhausted distinguishable from infrastructure_error at the moment it is written, not afterwards from a log.

report_status.$comment: The SAME four words as contracts/collect-vocabulary.json `statuses`, and both readers assert the two lists are equal. A fifth spelling here would let a cloud run and a herd run disagree about what happened to the same tick with nothing failing — which is the bug collect-vocabulary.json was written to stop.

schema_id.description: The role-specific contract `result` satisfies. Must equal the JobSpec.output_schema that asked for it.

result.description: The role-specific payload. Open here because its shape is the role contract named by schema_id, which the reconciler validates separately; the ENVELOPE around it is what this record freezes.

phase.$comment: The gate vocabulary the current implementation already runs (SPEC §6.1 Gates: 'configured worker/post-wave/integrated/review commands'), plus closeout. Naming the phase is what makes a record reproducible: the same command against the same ref at a different phase answers a different question. Reached through $defs.provenance, so a checkpoint, an attempt, a decision and an evidence record all name their phase from this one closed vocabulary.

check_result.$comment: `error` is not `fail`: a gate whose command could not run has produced no evidence about the source ref, and treating that as a failing test sends repair at the wrong thing.

acceptance.description: Whether this evidence gates closure or merely informs it. Recorded per-record because the same command is required at the integrated gate and advisory inside a worker.

inline_output.$comment: SPEC §10.1 says stdout/stderr are kept 'bounded and redacted'. Both are required booleans, so a record cannot be silent about whether it was cut short or whether secrets were stripped — the two questions a reader of old evidence always has.

provenance.description: Where a record came from: which run, which refs, which phase, and what produced it — SPEC §10.1's provenance fields. This is the ONE definition of them in the bundle. The evidence record below carries it, and so does every committed .ticfac/ record (contracts/ticfac-run-state.json, SPEC §10.4: 'every committed file carries a schema_version and the provenance fields of an evidence record'). Every field is REQUIRED, nullable where it can be genuinely absent: a record that omits integration_ref and one that states it as null are different claims, and only the second is evidence.

tick_id.description: Null for epic-level or run-level records.

attempt.description: Null for a record that belongs to no single dispatch — a run checkpoint, say.

integration_ref.description: Null before integration. Required-and-null rather than omitted, because 'this ran before integration' and 'nobody recorded where it ran' are different claims.

executor.description: Null for a record no executor produced — a reconciler-side decision, say.

backend.description: The concrete backend, e.g. container-shell. Backend names do not cross the JobSpec seam; a record names them AFTER the fact, which is how a run is explained without the reconciler ever choosing one.

role.description: Null for a deterministic check with no LLM behind it — a test command is evidence too.

evidence.$comment: THE ONE EVIDENCE RECORD. contracts/ticfac-run-state.json owns where this file goes (.ticfac/runs/<run-id>/evidence/<key>.json) and how it is written (create-if-absent against origin); it references this schema by schema_id rather than describing the record a second time. Bundle 1.2.0 shipped two incompatible shapes of it and neither reader noticed, because each validated its own examples — hence the cross-file readers that now validate both contracts' golden evidence examples against this definition.

key.description: The record's identity within its run, and its filename: .ticfac/runs/<run-id>/evidence/<key>.json (SPEC §10.4). A JobResult or a RoleResult cites evidence by this key — see evidence_ref.

exit_code.description: Null for a review check that ran no process.

golden.name: the SPEC illustration, verbatim
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — the illustrative JobSpec printed in the design document
golden.$comment: Byte-for-byte what §4.3 prints. It is the document a reader will copy first, so it is the one that must not quietly stop validating.

golden.name: a metered model grant with an explicit write grade
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'a metered credential carries a cost budget enforced from gateway telemetry'

golden.name: a flat-rate seat that states it has no budget
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'a flat-rate credential has no per-request cost to bound and says so'
golden.$comment: limits carries wall_seconds and NO max_cost_usd, and the grant states budget_field: null. Wall-clock and cancellation still bind it.

golden.name: a Cloudflare Computer handle
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'JobHandle is a stable, opaque, re-addressable identity'

golden.name: a local subprocess handle
golden.source: SPEC §12 Phase 1 — 'start is spawn; inspect is pid, worktree state, and RESULT'
golden.$comment: The same record, an entirely different payload. That is what `handle` being the one open object buys.

golden.name: a running job with a resumption cursor
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'JobStatus reports lifecycle observations and a cursor'

golden.name: a job the executor can no longer address
golden.$comment: `lost` with terminal: false. The controller must re-address or escalate; it must NOT dispose.

golden.name: a cancellation that revoked first
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'cancel MUST revoke those credentials before requesting a stop'

golden.name: a successful implement-tick collect
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'JobResult reports terminal facts, source refs, structured role output, and artifact/evidence references'

role_result.summary: Added the executor protocol schemas and both readers.

golden.name: a flat-rate seat that ran out of quota
golden.source: SPEC §4.3 — 'quota exhaustion is reported as its own failure class, never as a broken route'
golden.$comment: No commits, so head_sha is null and commits is 0 — stated, not inferred. The failure class is quota_exhausted, not infrastructure_error.

golden.name: a blocked implement-tick envelope
golden.source: SPEC §4.4 — 'every LLM call is a bounded job with a role-specific contract'
golden.$comment: BLOCKED is one of the four collect-vocabulary statuses. A worker can commit nothing and still return a well-formed envelope; the envelope is what the reconciler validates, the verdict is what it decides.

document.summary: The migration this tick depends on has not landed on the base ref.

decisions.question: Stub the missing migration or stop?
decisions.reason: A stub would pass the gate and hide the ordering bug the next wave inherits.

golden.name: an integrated gate that passed, output kept inline
a review-role check with no process, output spilled to an artifact
golden.source: SPEC §10.1 — 'stdout/stderr or artifact URI (bounded and redacted)'; SPEC §6.3 — review-epic runs against the integrated EpicRun ref and is required
golden.$comment: exit_code is null because nothing ran; role/model/profile_digest are set because an LLM did. The mirror image of the gate above, and the reason each of those fields is nullable rather than optional. It is EPIC-level, and the three fields that say so are load-bearing: SPEC §6.3 puts review-epic at the epic boundary, running read-only against the integrated ref, so tick_id is null (it belongs to no single tick), source_ref IS the integration ref rather than an attempt branch, and acceptance is `required` — there is no implementation-role fallback for a required frontier review. An earlier cut of this example had all three the other way and was a review-epic record no §6.3 review could have produced.

negative.name: a JobSpec with no credential grant
negative.why: Credentials are part of the protocol, not an adapter detail. A spec that names none is not 'unrestricted' — it is a job nobody can say afterwards what it was allowed to touch.

negative.name: a source grade outside the vocabulary
negative.why: The grade is the security boundary. An unrecognised grade must be refused, not treated as the nearest thing the issuer knows how to mint.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.credentials.source: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: a flat-rate credential that quietly carries a budget
negative.why: THE COST BUG THIS SCHEMA EXISTS FOR. A subscription seat has no per-request cost to enforce a budget against, so a budget on one is a number that looks enforced and is not. flat_rate_cost requires budget_field to be null, so this fails both alternatives instead of half-passing one.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.credentials.model: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: a role nobody wrote a contract for
negative.why: There is no universal Decision Agent (SPEC §4.4). A role outside the list has no prompt, no profile and no output contract, so dispatching it produces output nothing can validate.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.role: refactor-everything is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: a JobSpec naming a concrete backend
negative.why: Backend names do not cross this seam (SPEC §4.3). A spec that pins `container-shell` has chosen the Cloudflare executor for every host that reads it, which is the coupling the capability request exists to prevent.

negative.name: a handle flattened to a string
negative.why: The payload is opaque, not unstructured. A string handle cannot carry the fields a restarted controller needs to re-address the job, and 'opaque' is exactly the word that invites this mistake.

negative.name: a running job flagged terminal
negative.why: THE LIVENESS BUG. A controller that believes a running job is terminal disposes a live workspace; one that believes a finished job is live waits forever. state and terminal are cross-checked so the disagreement fails at the boundary.
negative.expect_error_contains: $: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: a cancellation that admits it did not revoke
negative.why: cancel MUST revoke credentials before requesting a stop. An acknowledgement is the only way a caller learns that happened, so `false` is not a status it may report — it is a refusal to have cancelled.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.credentials_revoked: false is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: a cancellation that stopped before revoking
negative.why: The ordering is the rule, not a detail: a job stopped first and revoked afterwards holds a live credential for the window in between, and a restart inside that window boots with it.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.order: stop-then-revoke is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: a cancelled handle that may ask again
negative.why: A kill switch is a durable refusal to ISSUE, checked before every boot — not a revocation a restart can undo. `retry-allowed` is that undo, spelled politely.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.reissue: retry-allowed is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: a failure with no failure class
negative.why: This is the record that produces 'the run broke' incident reports. Requiring the class at write time is what keeps quota_exhausted distinguishable from infrastructure_error later, when only the record survives.
negative.expect_error_contains: $: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: a success carrying a failure class
negative.why: The mirror of the above, and the one a hand-written adapter actually emits: a struct with every field set, serialized whole. A success that also names how it failed is two claims, and a reconciler branching on either one is right half the time.
negative.expect_error_contains: $: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: a role result with a status of its own invention
negative.why: THE VERDICT-INVERSION BUG collect-vocabulary.json was written to stop. A fifth spelling of 'done' makes a cloud run and a herd run disagree about what happened to the same tick, and nothing fails — the report just quietly means something else.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.status: COMPLETE is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: evidence that does not say which commit it ran against
negative.why: Evidence is 'a record that a check ran AGAINST A NAMED SOURCE REF' (SPEC §10.1). Without the sha it is a record that a check ran, which proves nothing about the tree anyone is about to merge.

negative.name: inline output that will not say whether it was redacted
negative.why: SPEC §10.1 requires output be bounded AND redacted. Both flags are required so an old record cannot be silent about the two questions its reader always has; silence here is how a token reaches an artifact store.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.output: value matches none of the anyOf alternatives

negative.name: evidence at a phase nobody gates on
negative.why: The phase is what makes a record reproducible — the same command against the same ref at a different phase answers a different question. An unknown phase silently joins no gate and blocks no closure.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.provenance.phase: smoke is not one of the permitted values

negative.name: the flat evidence record bundle 1.2.0 shipped
negative.why: THE REGRESSION CONTROL FOR THIS RECONCILIATION. In bundle 1.2.0 this document validated here while the run-state contract required a nested provenance object and a key, so no document could satisfy both and neither suite could see it — each validated its own examples against its own schema. Provenance is now one nested object, and the flat spelling is refused rather than accepted alongside it.

negative.name: evidence accepted under a vocabulary this contract does not publish
negative.why: The other half of the same reconciliation: the run-state golden example said acceptance was "accepted", which is a RESULT dressed as an acceptance. Acceptance says whether the record gates closure (required) or merely informs it (advisory); whether it passed is `result`. Two vocabularies for one field is how a gate stops gating without anything failing.
negative.expect_error_contains: $.acceptance: accepted is not one of the permitted values
